about: Ceilings for scripts/perf/measure.mjs --check (medians, headless Chromium on an Apple M1 Pro GPU, 1440×900 at 2x, wheel scrolling from 0.7 s). Times in ms. Baseline (8 Oct 2026, before the performance series): first visit froze 3.4–4.6 s at desk ready with 53 shader programs; returning visits had one ~190 ms frame. Each PR of the series lowers its ceilings as it lands (docs/qa/perf). Desk warm-up: first visit 898 ms (the reflective floor's blur still compiles in the hidden frame). Marble without a live mirror: first visit 469 ms (About mounting); 36 programs. Butter series (9 Oct 2026, docs/qa/perf/butter-baseline.md): trackpad input (6–30 px every 8–16 ms) adds ceilings per scenario at the baseline; each PR of the series lowers them. Butter final (9 Oct 2026, live site, docs/qa/perf/butter-final.md): the trackpad ceilings drop to the new levels with headroom. Final revisions (15 Nov 2026): the program ceiling follows main, which had grown from 36 to 43–44 by then (41 already at the butter final); the series itself adds none (docs/qa/perf/final-baseline.md and final-after.md both count 44). Flow series (16 Nov 2026, docs/qa/perf/flow-*): ceilings per class of computer under `profiles`, read by `npm run perf:check -- --profile <name>`. They hold what the series reached with headroom: an even desk on 120 Hz displays (frames paced to every second refresh), integrated graphics within a 60 Hz frame on the low tier, and slow frames on an old processor where they were. Uneven About frames are not held with a notched wheel: About mixes its 30 fps idle sway with full-rate frames by design.
